test1_money_vs_price.verdict: FAIL/WEAK: money variables alone do not rank 2010–2024 nominal house-price growth across the 12 markets (rho ≈ 0.15–0.22). Largest wrong-way points: MY (highest real rate, near-top price growth), KR (high M2, near-bottom growth), HK (lowest real rate, mid growth). Supports the framework only in its full form: money without the institutional/supply terms has no cross-sectional ranking power.

spearman_excl_JP.reason: BOJ did not tighten; natural experiment condition absent

test2_downside_stickiness.verdict: SUPPORTED (moderate): among markets that actually tightened, higher floating-rate share ranks with deeper 2021–24 nominal drawdowns (rho −0.68, n=7). MY annotation: predominantly floating yet max drawdown −0.2% — the institutional-stickiness residual (HDA, developer holding) the framework predicts.

test5_state_classification.question: Can the pre-declared state rules (SPEC N) classify markets as primed/capped IN ADVANCE, with primed delivering systematically better forward 3-5y returns?

rules_as_applied.S1: volume/inventory series at <=30th percentile of own trailing 10y (midrank percentile); fixed series per market: US = months supply of new houses (FRED MSACSR), UK = HMLR sales volume, TW = MOI transfer registrations; others N/A
rules_as_applied.S2: mortgage rate at <=20th percentile of own trailing 10y; series: US MORTGAGE30US, AU RBA F5 FILRHLBVS, CA BoC V80691335 5y conventional, UK BoE IUMTLMV SVR, TW CBC 5-bank new housing loan rate, MY BNM ALR (2008+); NZ/JP N/A. The yield-carry alternative was used nowhere (no verified historical yield series)
rules_as_applied.S3_C2: BIS total credit to households %GDP via FRED Q**HAM770A, Q4 values; S3 = fall >=3pp vs T-5; C2 = level >=80 or rise >=5pp vs T-5; TW N/A (not a BIS reporter)
rules_as_applied.S4_C3: price-to-income = OECD HPI_YDH annual mean (US/UK/AU/NZ/CA/JP), TW = MOI 房價所得比; S4 = below own trailing-15y median; C3 = >=15% above it; MY N/A
rules_as_applied.C1: inventory >=70th pct of trailing 10y — only the US has an inventory-type series (MSACSR); all others N/A
rules_as_applied.classification: primed: S>=3 & C<=1; capped: C>=2 & S<=1; else neutral. N/A scores 0 and is counted; markets with fewer than 3 computable S-rules can never reach primed (TW has 3, MY/NZ/JP have 2) — disclosed, not patched
rules_as_applied.forward_returns: BIS nominal index annual averages (TW: Sinyi Q4), T to T+3 / T+5, judgment years 2000-2021

calibration_checks.US_2019: NOT primed (S=1/4: rates not bottom-quintile, volumes not compressed, PTI at median; only S3 hit). The rules missed the 2019-2021 US boom. Reported as-is.
calibration_checks.TW_2019: NOT primed (S=1/3: volumes had already recovered by 2019 so S1=0, PTI above 15y median so S4=0; S2 hit). TW 2016-2018 came closest at S=2/3 with S3 unavailable (TW not a BIS credit reporter). Reported as-is.
calibration_checks.MY_2016_2020: Never formally capped: only C2 computable for MY (C max 1 < threshold 2). C2 fired 2014-2016 and 2020; forward 3y returns then fell to 4.6-9.0% for T=2017-2020 judgments, directionally consistent with the site thesis, but the strict rules cannot issue the capped label. Insufficient data, disclosed.
calibration_checks.JP_all_years: Never primed (S1/S2 unavailable caps S at 2 - a data limitation, disclosed) and never capped (deleveraging kept C2=0; post-crash PTI kept C3=0). The deflation-era declines (2000-2008, f3 -2 to -17%) therefore sit in the NEUTRAL bucket: the rules did not catch Japan falling, and could not have caught Japan rising. Falsification verdict: no false signal issued on Japan, but no skill demonstrated either.

honest_verdict.as_upside_finder: WEAK. Only 5 primed cases in 176 market-years, all US 2011-2016. Median 3y forward: primed 17.9% vs neutral 17.4% - no separation. 35 neutral cases delivered 3y >= 30% that the rules did not catch (early-2000s Anglosphere, post-COVID US/NZ/TW).
honest_verdict.as_false_positive_filter: STRONG in-sample. Zero primed cases below +10% at 3y; primed IQR tight (17.7-22.3) and all positive at both horizons.
honest_verdict.as_downside_classifier: PARTIAL. The only market-years with all three C-rules firing (US 2005-2007, C=3/3) preceded the only systemic crash in sample (f3 -15 to -27%). But 33 of 49 capped cases still returned >= +10% over 3y: the C2 debt-level trigger (>=80% GDP) marks AU/NZ/CA as capped for decades while they compounded. As written, capped means better-avoided tails (q1 +2.4% vs neutral q1 +7.7%), not falling prices.
honest_verdict.overall: The state machine, applied with pre-declared thresholds and no tuning, is an honest but narrow tool: it reliably avoids bad primed calls and it flagged the one true bust, but it finds few opportunities and mislabels chronically-leveraged compounders as capped. The thresholds were NOT adjusted after seeing these results, per the iron rules.

regime_conditioning.regime_rule: G3 central bank total assets (Fed WALCL, ECB ECBASSETSW, BOJ JPNASSETS via FRED; PBoC/BoE not available on FRED - G3 used, disclosed), year-end 12-month change converted to USD at annual-average FX (FRED DEXUSEU/DEXJPUS), divided by combined US+euro-area+Japan nominal GDP (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD). Thresholds fixed before computing: >+5% = easing, <-2% = tightening, else normal. Coverage 2003-2024 (WALCL starts Dec 2002; 2000-2002 N/A).
honest_notes: The rule was expected to also catch 2009 and 2012-13. It does not: 2009 prints -0.95% (Fed assets roughly flat year-end-to-year-end after the late-2008 spike, which the rule dates as easing-2008), and 2012-13 print +0.7%/+1.7% (ECB balance-sheet contraction offset Fed QE3). Reported as-is; thresholds not adjusted.
USD conversion embeds FX valuation effects: yen depreciation deepens the measured 2022 tightening.
regime_conditioning.strata_note: all_normal = forward 3y window entirely in normal years; crosses_regime = window overlaps at least one easing or tightening year; windows touching 2000-2002 (regime unknown) excluded. Every judgment year 2017-2021 has its forward window inside the 2020-2024 regime storm.
regime_conditioning.reading: Primed-vs-neutral separation is clearer in all-normal windows (22.3 vs 16.6 median). The capped bucket is harmless in normal windows (median 20.6) and does its damage where windows cross regimes (q1 -1.2): busts in this sample happen around regime shifts, not in calm conditions.
regime_conditioning.us2019_reframed: Under the regime frame, the correct statement of the US-2019 miss is: the framework should not be asked to predict a global liquidity flood, but it should be able to rank who rises most when the flood arrives.

easing_window_cross_section.dependent: nominal HPI change 2019Q4 to 2021Q4, BIS quarterly (TW: Sinyi Q4), 12 markets

cohort_25_39_momentum_2015_2020.source: UN World Population Prospects 2024, PopulationByAge5Group medium/estimates CSV, ages 25-39 both sexes

easing_window_cross_section.reading: Same flood, different boats: the 2020-21 rise ranks best on young-cohort momentum (rho +0.44; NZ top on both, JP/HK/TH bottom), ahead of money growth (+0.29) and the real rate (-0.12, right sign, negligible). Taiwan is the clear wrong-way point (cohort shrinking, prices +22%), suggesting a money-substitute demand channel the slow variables do not carry. First calibration of the v2 slow layer: moderate, not strong.

test6_turn_sequencing.question: At verifiable historical turning points, does the transmission chain credit -> volume -> price hold, with what lead, and does stickiness (Test 2) shape the post-top price path?

rules_as_applied.hard_top: local max (strictly above previous 4 and at-or-above next 4 quarters) followed by a decline of >=8% within 12 quarters, on the nominal quarterly index
rules_as_applied.hard_bottom: local min preceded by a >=8% decline from the prior peak and followed by a >=8% rise within 12 quarters
rules_as_applied.soft_top: first quarter with price YoY < 2% where YoY exceeded 8% within the previous 8 quarters (8-quarter lookback is an implementation constant, declared); deduplicated within 8 quarters
rules_as_applied.volume_turn: YoY of the 4-quarter moving average of volume changes sign and holds the new sign for >=2 quarters
rules_as_applied.credit_turn: local peak/trough of mortgage-stock YoY over a +/-4-quarter window, deduplicated within 4 quarters
rules_as_applied.lead: price turn quarter minus nearest same-direction volume/credit turn within +/-12 quarters, SIGNED. Disclosure: the first implementation matched only non-negative leads (a bias toward confirming leads); it was corrected to signed nearest-match before results were interpreted, and the signed version is the only one reported

sources.prices: BIS via FRED (US/GB/NZ/MY, full history); TW = MOI national housing price index, official quarterly PDF 114Q4, parsed 2012Q3-2025Q4 (https://pip.moi.gov.tw/Upload/CustomFile/Doc/114Q4住宅價格指數統計成果.pdf)

sources.volume_GB: HM Land Registry UK HPI SalesVolume, monthly 2005-2024 (spec named HMRC; HMLR is the official transaction count in hand, disclosed)

volume_to_price.reading: volume-leads-price does NOT hold as a general rule under the 4-quarter-MA dating; the smoothing eats the lead at hard tops. Leads concentrate at soft tops (US 1990Q4 +5, GB 2023Q2 +4)

credit_to_price.reading: credit is the only link in the chain that holds: mortgage-stock YoY peaked at or before 8 of 10 price turns (US 2006Q1 lead 0, GB 2007Q3 +2; bottoms US 2011Q1 +1, GB 2012Q1 +4). If one builds a property clock, the hand is credit, not volume

zero_hard_turns_finding.TW: zero hard tops and zero hard bottoms over the full official index (2012Q3-2025Q4); the 2014-16 episode registers only as a soft top (2015Q4) with +1.0% price path 8 quarters on
zero_hard_turns_finding.MY: 27 years without a single 8% drawdown since the Asian Financial Crisis (last hard top 1997Q2, last bottom 1999Q1); the 2012-13 deceleration took ~24 quarters to travel from >8% YoY to <2%, outrunning the 8-quarter lookback, so no soft top triggers
zero_hard_turns_finding.reading: this is a finding, not a defect: in sticky/institutionally damped markets the top takes the form of volume and momentum disappearing while the price barely moves - consistent with the Test 2 stickiness grouping. Volume is not a leading indicator of price there; volume IS the turn

top_shape_8q.note: US 2006Q4 soft top is the same GFC event as the 2006Q1 hard top, dated later by the YoY rule

calibration_checks.US_2012_bottom: dated 2011Q1 by the rule on the BIS series - one year earlier than the expected 2012; reported as dated
calibration_checks.TW_2014_soft_top: dated 2015Q4 - four quarters later than expected (national YoY did not fall below 2% until then)
calibration_checks.TW_2019_bottom: NOT TRIGGERABLE - no >=8% decline ever existed on the index, so the bottom rule has nothing to fire on; the 2019 turn is visible only in volume and momentum
calibration_checks.MY_2012_13_soft_top: NOT TRIGGERED - the deceleration was too gradual for the written rule; recorded as an institutional-damping finding, not patched
calibration_checks.NZ_2021_top: HIT - hard top dated 2021Q4, price -11.3% eight quarters on

v2_calibration.preregistration: SPEC P is the pre-registration document; rules below were fixed before computation and were NOT adjusted after seeing results. Historical runs are labelled CALIBRATION, not evidence (answers were known); the true test is the 2026 forward freeze scored in 2029.

rules.SL1: population aged 25-39, change T to T+5 (UN WPP 2024, actuals for calibration): >+3% = +1, <-3% = -1, else 0
rules.SL2: 10-year cumulative (household formation - completions) / housing stock: >+2% = +1, <-2% = -1, else 0. Computable only for the US in Phase A (FRED TTLHH households, COMPUTSA completions, ETOTALUSQ176N stock); GB/AU/NZ/CA expected computable but not verified this phase - N/A scored 0, disclosed
rules.SL3: one-time institutional constant: vacancy <5% = +1; vacancy >8% AND effective property tax >=0.5% = -1; vacancy >8% AND tax <0.3% = 0 (vacancy is not effective supply); else 0. Headline official vacancy measure used uniformly
rules.FL1: mortgage-credit YoY local trough followed by >=2 rising quarters = +1 (ignition) in the confirmation year; local peak followed by >=2 falling quarters = -1; computable US/GB only (Test 6 credit series)
rules.classes: primed_v2: slow>=+2; ignited: slow>=+2 and FL1=+1; capped_v2: slow<=-1; else neutral
rules.KPI: same-year cross-market rank of forward 3y nominal gain (rank percentile, 0=best), per the Test 1 lesson: ranks not levels

US.vacancy: 10.3% gross vacancy (Census HVS 2024, incl. ~4pp seasonal/vacation - a rule-letter artifact, disclosed: year-round-only would read ~7-8% and score 0)

JP.vacancy: 13.8% 空き家率 (住宅・土地統計調査 2023)
JP.tax: 固定資産税+都市計画税, effective >=0.5%

TW.vacancy: 9.79% 低度使用(用電)住宅 (內政部)
TW.tax: effective holding tax <0.3% - vacancy does not constitute effective supply (the institutionalised Taiwan counterexample)

sl3_constants.others: AU/NZ/CA/KR/SG/HK/TH not verified in Phase A - N/A scored 0, to be filled or permanently disclosed in Phase B

calibration_five.US_2011_13: v1 hit LOST in v2: SL1=+1 (millennial influx) but SL2=0 (cumulative gap never crosses the pre-registered +/-2%: -1.5% to -0.5%) and SL3=-1 (the US gross-vacancy artifact) -> slow 0, neutral. Reported as calibration regression, rules not adjusted.
calibration_five.US_2019: the key test FAILS, and worse than v1: SL1=0 (25-39 cohort change 2019->2024 = -0.03% on WPP actuals - the millennial-peak premise is factually wrong for 25-39 by 2019), SL2=0 (+1.6%, below +2%), SL3=-1 -> slow -1 = capped_v2, then ranked 2nd of 12 with +38.6%. v2 wrong-ways its flagship case.
calibration_five.TW_2019: as pre-predicted, not caught - and worse, mislabelled: SL1=-1 (-12.1%), SL3=0 -> capped_v2, then ranked 4th of 12 (+31.4%). Confirms the known boundary: the Taiwan driver is repatriated capital (factor five), which v2 does not carry.
calibration_five.JP: the one clear v2 win: slow<=-1 through the deflation years (SL1<=0, SL3=-1), so Japan is finally classified capped - and correctly: JP 2003 ranked 12/12, 2008 10/12. v1 could not classify Japan at all.
calibration_five.MY: SL1=+1 every year (cohort growth +6.7% to +12%), SL2/SL3 N/A -> slow +1, neutral throughout. Insufficient inputs, disclosed.

v2_calibration.honest_verdict: As pre-registered, the v2 slow layer is a BOTTOM-HALF FILTER, not a top finder: capped_v2 (n=80) has a median same-year rank percentile of 0.75 vs 0.50 for neutral - the negative side of the asymmetry works, with Japan finally classified correctly. The positive side fails in calibration: only GB ever reaches slow>=+2 (2012-2015, mid-table outcomes, one ignited case n=1), the US 2011-13 v1 hit is lost to the SL3 vacancy-metric artifact, and both flagship 2019 cases are wrong-wayed. Two structural causes, both disclosed: SL2 is data-starved (1 of 12 markets) and never fires at the pre-registered +/-2%; SL3 gross-vacancy penalises the US for seasonal homes. Rules stand as registered; the 2026 freeze proceeds with these caveats printed beside it.

test7_supply.question: Do supply elasticity (published estimates) or a self-computed supply-gap explain the 2010-2024 cross-market price ranking, and does money x supply beat money alone (completing the Test 1 hypothesis)?

test7_supply.verdict: NOT SCORABLE THIS ROUND. The published cross-country elasticity tables (Caldera-Johansson 2013; Cavalleri et al. 2019) are locked behind paywalls, 403 walls or exist only as charts in every accessible copy; transcribing from memory or unverifiable search snippets violates the data rules. The self-computed gap variable is computable for too few markets (1-3) to correlate. After three attempts across this study (Test 1 phase, BIS QR excerpt, Test 7), the supply factor remains the framework's known open flank: unverified, not refuted.

The positive side (primed/ignited) had insufficient calibration evidence (n<=3, mid-table outcomes) and both 2019 flagship cases were wrong-wayed. Read the table accordingly.
v2_frozen_2026.na_policy: Sub-scores that could not be verified are N/A (not zero-filled into a hard call); markets with fewer than 2 of 3 computable slow components are classed insufficient_inputs, not judged.

us_pilot.strategy: US single-market depth pilot. Train 1975-1999 (only place where tuning is allowed, fully logged) -> freeze -> test 2000-2025 exactly once. Test period NOT touched in Phase A.

data_sources.price: FHFA all-transactions HPI, FRED USSTHPI, 1975Q1- (Case-Shiller CSUSHPINSA 1987- retained as cross-check)
data_sources.volume: Census new one-family houses sold HSN1F (NAR history unavailable on FRED, disclosed) + months supply MSACSR
data_sources.credit: Z.1 home mortgage liabilities HHMSDODNS, quarterly YoY
data_sources.supply_stock: HOUST, COMPUTSA, TTLHH (census-break caveat carried over), homeowner vacancy RHVRUSQ156N (fixes the v2 gross-vacancy defect)
data_sources.cohort: UN WPP 2024 ages 25-39 (auxiliary series, not in the tension score)
data_sources.valuation: USSTHPI / per-capita nominal disposable income (A229RC0Q052SBEA) - basis declared; median-income series only starts 1984, so DPI per capita chosen for full-sample uniformity

structure_frozen.tension_score: 0-4: homeowner vacancy <= P_low pctile of trailing 40q; months supply <= P_low pctile; 10-yr cumulative (formation-completions) > 0; valuation < trailing-40q median. Components with <32 of 40 quarters available score 0 (early-sample valuation windows)
structure_frozen.FL1_state: credit YoY local extremes (+/-4q, dedup 4q), confirmation at extreme+2q; state machine: rising from trough-confirmation, falling from peak-confirmation
structure_frozen.phases: precedence fixed: overheat > ignition > primed > cooling. overheat = hpi YoY >= P_hi pctile (40q) AND valuation > K2 x trailing median; ignition = tension >= K1 and credit rising; primed = tension >= K1 and credit not rising; cooling = credit falling
structure_frozen.annual_inputs: gap uses annual values held constant within the year (declared, not interpolation)

tuning_log.grid: K1 in {2,3}, P_low in {20,30,40}, P_hi in {70,80}, K2 in {1.0,1.05,1.10} = 36 trials, all recorded
tuning_log.objective: A = median fwd-12q return (primed+ignition) minus (overheat+cooling), judgments to 1996Q4; B = +5 if 1988-89 mode phase is overheat, +5 if 1992-94 mode is primed/cooling; C = -100 if phase coverage < 50%. Ties broken by first-in-grid order (most permissive config)
honest_notes: OVERHEAT NEVER FIRES in training under any grid config: the P_hi/K2 columns are degenerate (identical scores across K2). The national FHFA index dilutes the bicoastal late-80s boom and the valuation ratio stayed below its trailing median, so the overheat structure cannot describe the 1988-89 episode at national level. Structure is frozen per spec; recorded as a known limitation going into the test period.
B scored 5 of 10: the 1992-94 stagnation check passed (mode primed/cooling), the 1988-89 overheat check failed.
1989Q1-1989Q4 mislabelled primed immediately before the 1990 top - a training-period wrong-way signal, recorded.

What the chosen config does describe correctly: cooling through 1979Q3-1982Q3 (the rate-shock pullback), primed 1982Q4 -> ignition 1983Q3 (the recovery), primed/ignition through 1992-1998 (the long early-90s repair and late-90s upturn).

training_results.timeline_compact: 1975-1979Q2 none/warmup | 1979Q3-1982Q3 cooling | 1982Q4 primed -> 1983Q3-1986Q1 ignition | 1986-1987 mixed | 1987Q4-1988 cooling | 1989 primed (wrong-way, noted) | 1990-1991 cooling | 1992-1995 primed/ignition | 1996Q3-1999 ignition/primed

us_pilot.phase_status: Phase A complete: data + training calibration + tuning log. AWAITING REVIEW. Test period 2000-2025 will be run exactly once after approval; results published regardless of outcome, no second pass.

test_period.one_shot_declaration: The 2000-2025 test period was run EXACTLY ONCE on 2026-07-12 with the frozen config (K1=2, P_low=20, P_hi=70, K2=1.0). This test set is now consumed: any future rule revision must declare test contamination and cannot re-use this period as out-of-sample evidence.

primary_nominal.verdict: WEAK on the union metric (+3.8pp): the up-group edge is diluted because overheat quarters (n=42) still returned +19% median. The separation that IS strong is cooling vs everything: cooling median -7.9% (q1 -13.1) against +16% to +40% for all other phases. The clock is better at saying get out than pick the moment.

supplementary_real_cpi_deflated.note: supplementary disclosure, not the primary metric (training used nominal); ordering identical, cooling gap widens

bottom_2011_12.verdict: MISS/LAG - the clock confirmed the bottom, it did not anticipate it

freeze_2022.note: FHFA national nominal never produced a hard or soft price top in 2022-24 (YoY fell 17%->~3% but not below 2%), so there is no price turn to measure against. Against the event (the 2022Q3 mortgage-rate shock) the clock reached cooling 2023Q2, roughly 3 quarters after; it also flickered overheat 2024Q1 and cooling again 2024Q2-Q4.

tracked_limitation_overheat_at_bubble.question: training could never light overheat; what did the clock show at the 2004-06 bubble top?
tracked_limitation_overheat_at_bubble.answer: OVERHEAT LIT CONTINUOUSLY 2003Q4-2006Q2 (valuation above trailing median with K2=1.0 and YoY >=70th pctile), then flipped to cooling 2006Q3, two quarters before the price top. The single most important observation of the test: the structure that was untunable in training (a degenerate parameter) fired correctly at national scale in the one episode that mattered.
tracked_limitation_overheat_at_bubble.caveat: this is the overheat rule's FIRST and ONLY validation - one episode; K2=1.0 was chosen by tie-break, not by training evidence. And overheat is a state, not a timer: it stayed lit for 10 quarters before the top in 2003-06, and lit again 2016-2018 and 2021-2023 with benign outcomes.

current_reading_2026Q1.note: zero tension components lit (vacancy and months-supply off lows, gap negative, valuation above median) while credit rises - consistent with the v2 freeze finding of ignition-on-negative-tension. The pilot rules also give the US no phase today.

test_period.honest_summary: One-shot verdict: the pilot PARTIALLY passes. Coverage 87% (pass). Turn detection 1 hit (2006 top, +2q lead), 1 miss (2011-12 bottom, 3-7q late), 1 ambiguous (2022 freeze, no price turn to score). Phase separation weak on the pre-declared union metric (+3.8pp nominal, +4.5pp real) but strong and clean on the cooling side (-7.9% vs +16~40% everything else). The clock as calibrated is an exit instrument, not an entry timer. Rules now frozen and contaminated for this period; next step per strategy is transplant to market #2 (Taiwan) rather than re-tuning.

instrument_series.note: per-quarter dashboard series behind the clock page panel: tension score with component booleans [vacancy, months-supply, gap, valuation], mortgage-credit YoY and FL1 state (r=rising/f=falling), plus ignition/extinction confirmation quarters. Recomputed deterministically from the frozen pipeline (verified identical to the stored test t-values).

test8_compass.question: Does the Compass (momentum x credit, four cells, from the Property Clock) rank forward 3-year nominal house-price returns in the order declared before reading any outcome: Fuelled >= Draining >= Reflating >= Starved?
test8_compass.theory: Momentum is the dominant axis (price trend persists); credit direction is the secondary tie-break within each trend direction. Not fitted: this ordering is stated before the medians below were read.
test8_compass.method: Per market, the realized 3-year forward nominal return is taken from data/compass-<m>.json qstat (median + n per cell, computed by scripts/build_compass.py over each cell's full quarterly history). Two measures: (1) pairwise concordance of the 4 cell medians against the 6 declared inequalities; (2) quarter-level Spearman rank correlation between the declared cell rank (fuelled=4 best .. starved=1 worst) and that quarter's realized fwd12, over all quarters with non-null fwd12 (warmup quarters excluded). Verdict thresholds fixed before reading results: rho>=0.3 holds, 0.10-0.30 weak, <0.10 breaks. Computed by scripts/backtest_compass.py.
test8_compass.source: data/compass-us.json, compass-tw.json, compass-my.json, compass-jp.json (built by scripts/build_compass.py from clock-<m>.json, already-collected series — no raw data refetched for this test); scripts/backtest_compass.py
test8_compass.in_sample_caveat: The cell->forward-return mapping (qstat) is measured on the same history the compass signal is built on (US/JP 1975-2026, TW 2001-2026, MY 2000-2026). The signal itself is trailing (momentum/credit z use only data <= t, no look-ahead within a quarter), but the ORDERING has not been tested out-of-sample -- only against history. The 2026 forward freeze below is the genuine out-of-sample test.
test8_compass.rank_not_timing: This predicts the ORDERING of returns across the four regimes, not the level or turning point of any single quarter. A market can be correctly ranked worst (starved) and still post a positive 3-year return, or ranked best (fuelled) and still underperform its own history -- see US and JP, where the ordering holds but fuelled and reflating medians sit within 0.4-3.7pp of each other.

US.note: Starved correctly ranks worst (min median); fuelled and reflating swap by 0.4pp (reflating n=19 vs fuelled n=70) -- the near-miss is a thin-cell artifact, not a reversal.

TW.note: Starved is the BEST cell (34.1%), not the worst -- a genuine inversion, not a near-miss. Taiwan 2001-2026 is a short, nearly one-directional bull run (see Test 6: zero hard tops/bottoms in its history); almost every downtrend quarter was simply followed by the next leg up. Sample problem, not a method problem.

MY.note: Fuelled correctly ranks best (max median), draining second; reflating and starved swap (8.2 vs 11.7, both thin cells, n=7 and n=24) -- the bottom two are close and out of order, top structure intact.

JP.note: Starved correctly ranks worst (-7.3%, the only negative-median cell alongside draining) -- Japan is the market that actually crashed, and starved captures it. Fuelled and reflating swap (6.0 vs 9.7), the same thin-cell pattern as the US.

test8_compass.overall_verdict: HOLDS in the US, Malaysia and Japan (rho 0.40-0.71); BREAKS in Taiwan (rho 0.081, and the pairwise ordering is inverted at the extremes -- its 'starved' cell has the single highest realized median of any cell in any market). The break is diagnosed, not hidden: Taiwan's 2001-2026 sample is short and nearly one-directional (zero hard tops or bottoms per Test 6), so almost every momentum-down quarter was simply followed by the next leg of one long bull run. This is a sample problem, not evidence against the mechanism -- but it is reported exactly as found.
